body:
## Summary
Four foundry gates (forge cull, extract, Dojo, strips) each carry a copy of the same verdict writer. Each one reads the manifest, filters the map and replaces verdicts.json whole: last writer wins, with no lock and no history. Replace the four with one kernel, lib/foundry/verdictLog.ts. It applies keyed PATCHes against a revision and answers 409 on a stale base. It runs under a per-run lock that the commit also holds. Every decision is appended to verdicts.log.jsonl with who made it and from which surface.

## Description
This adopts the open foundry-engine-B card and the 2026-10-07 critic's fold-in of `by`, and widens both: the strips gate (22b439f) made it four copies. The kernel is generic over the record shape: patchVerdicts<R>(spec, id, {set, clear, baseRev, by, surface}). `spec` is each store's {dir, known(manifest), clean(record) or refuse, isCommitted(manifest)}. The four putXVerdicts become adapters a few lines long. PUT stays as a deprecated whole-map write: it diffs against the current map and logs only the keys that changed. The per-run lock comes from lib/diskTx.ts (exclusiveSection on <runDir>/.verdicts.lock). commitRun, commitExtractRun, commitCycle and commitStripRun take it before withCatalogue, so there is one lock order (run, then catalogue) and the window where a verdict write lands between a commit's read and its committed stamp closes. ExtractVerdictRecord gains note and reasons. VerdictRecord gains by?: 'human'|'model'. `proven` counts human keeps only, in both commitRun and planForgeCommit, so preview still equals commit. GET returns rev.

## Flow
- PATCH {set|clear, baseRev, by, surface}: the route validates the shape; the kernel takes the run lock, reads the manifest (committed gives 409), then reads {rev, map} (baseRev not equal to rev gives 409 {rev})
- each key goes through the store's clean(); one log line is appended per changed key; the map is written at rev+1; the lock is released
- commit: run lock, then withCatalogue, then read verdicts, plan, write and stamp committed, then release both. A PATCH that was waiting on the lock sees committed and gets 409
- PUT: the same path with baseRev = current and set = the diff

## Expected impact
- One rule replaces four drifting copies.
- The Board's client-side read-fresh workaround (lib/board/sources/cull.ts:3-7) stops being load-bearing. Moving foundryClient to PATCH is a small follow-up in foundry-curation.
- Extract reject reasons stop being dropped.
- The gate's decision history (who, from which surface, in what order) survives the commit that deletes the media. That is the data calibration needs, and its card (foundry-curation-B) is held for lack of it.
- A model keep can no longer promote a style to proven.

## Evaluation
Claim: verdict writes are keyed, revisioned, logged and fenced against commit on all four gates
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (case 8 is a [guard] on the PUT half)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - tests/golden-path/foundry-verdict-patch.probe.spec.ts on OUT_ROOT/FOUNDRY_DIR temp roots, the race driven in both orders by the tests/golden-path/_effects.ts Interleaver, plus the existing foundry-* and board probes, then npm run typecheck
Result: better
Gate: contract (in-tree: the request shape of four routes, verified by foundry-routes and the new probe; the only external caller, app/foundry/foundryClient.ts, keeps working on PUT)

title: Extract runs meter their own spend: per-run ceiling, budget stop parks not trips
acceptance: runToEnd with a fake EngineIO whose Served results carry costUsd (recognize 0.002, generate 0.04, reason 0.01) -> m.spend.usd equals the exact sum of every served call, m.spend.by_stage has read/group/replica/transfer subtotals that sum to it, m.spend.unpriced is 0

same fake with options.ceilingUsd 0.10 -> no unit is started once spend.usd + that unit's declared estimate would exceed the ceiling: status 'failed', m.stopped = {by:'run-ceiling', spentUsd, ceilingUsd}, spend.usd <= 0.10, zero Served calls after the stop, fail_streak unchanged

fake generate throws ImagingError kind 'over-budget' on the first replica -> run stops with m.stopped.by 'period-ceiling', NO ReplicaRound is appended, fail_streak stays 0, m.error does not say 'consecutive vendor failures' (today engine.ts:423-427 appends an errored round and tripped() counts it toward BREAKER_LIMIT)

a run stopped by 'run-ceiling' with no failed unit -> stepRun(id, 1, true, {ceilingUsd: 0.50}) on a temp EXTRACT_ROOT resumes: status back to a live stage, stopped cleared, one unit performed (today pruneFailures returns 0 at engine.ts:155 and the run stays 'failed' with no way back)
a Served result with costUsd undefined -> spend.unpriced increments and spend.usd adds that unit's pre-call estimate with basis 'estimate', so an unpriced vendor cannot run past the ceiling for free
listExtractRuns() summaries carry spendUsd; commitExtractRun writes run.committed.spendUsd and costPerKeptUsd = spendUsd / kept.length

rollback: Two commits (test, then feat). spend and stopped are optional manifest fields: an old manifest reads as unmetered and an absent ceiling is explicitly unlimited, so reverting the feat commit leaves every run on disk readable. The ceiling is opt-in per run (options.ceilingUsd); the default path does not change behaviour (case 7).
runner_up: Turn the extract step machine into a server-side drain job on the local posture (lease-holding loop, browser-driven only on Cloud Run) so closing the tab stops nothing - weaker, because the lease plus the CLI loop already cover long runs.

body:
## Summary
The extract engine is the one foundry gate that spends money without counting it. liveIO throws away every call's costUsd and the manifest has no spend field. A refusal from the period budget is booked as a vendor failure, so it trips the breaker, and a run stopped for money cannot be resumed. The move: meter spend on the manifest, enforce a per-run ceiling in the scheduler, and treat a budget refusal as a named stop instead of a failure.

## Description
The engine's Served<T> gains costUsd? and basis, and liveIO passes them through from provenance. step() books every served call into m.spend = {usd, by_stage, unpriced, basis}. ExtractOptions gains ceilingUsd?, clamped in newManifest; absent means unlimited, and the code says so explicitly. Before performing a unit, the scheduler compares spend.usd plus the unit's declared estimate against the ceiling. A unit that would cross it is not started, and the run stops with stopped = {by:'run-ceiling', spentUsd, ceilingUsd}. An over-budget ImagingError or TextError caught inside a unit no longer goes to tripped(). It stops the run with stopped.by = 'period-ceiling' and leaves no failed element behind. The resume path clears stopped, and /step accepts {retry, ceilingUsd} to raise the ceiling and continue. The commit stamps spendUsd and costPerKeptUsd, the number cost-per-usable-economics asks for.

## Flow
- a liveIO call returns Served{value, model, costUsd, basis}; step books the spend under its stage (an unpriced call books its estimate and bumps a counter)
- the scheduler picks the next unit; if spend + estimate > ceiling it calls stop(run-ceiling), otherwise it performs the unit
- a vendor throw of kind over-budget calls stop(period-ceiling) and leaves fail_streak alone; any other throw goes to tripped() as today
- POST /step {retry:true, ceilingUsd} clears stopped, raises the ceiling and continues at the next unit
- the commit records committed.spendUsd and costPerKeptUsd

## Expected impact
An operator can start a sixty-image extraction with a dollar ceiling and know it stops there. A budget wall no longer reads as three vendor failures, and it no longer burns rounds that a retry then has to prune. Extract joins Dojo and Strips in recording what a kept style cost, so a later cull can rank by cost per keep.

## Evaluation
Claim: extract spend is metered and ceilinged per run, and a budget refusal stops the run cleanly and resumably
Before: 0 of 7 cases pass (case 7 is [guard], green before by design)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - tests/golden-path/extract-spend.probe.spec.ts drives engine step/runToEnd with a priced fake EngineIO (the style-extract probe's pattern) and stepRun on a temp EXTRACT_ROOT for case 4; then npm run typecheck and the existing extract/foundry probes
Result: better
Gate: none

Sequencing note: shares lib/foundry/extract/store.ts and lib/foundry/extract/types.ts with this context's slot-A card (different functions: liveIO/stepRun vs putExtractVerdicts). Do not put both in one wave.
